# Purpose of this overview

The September 2026 Plan Team package brings together three working papers on
RTMB, SPoRC, and Rceattle. Each addresses a different development question.
This page explains how the papers fit together, where their results agree, and
what guidance is requested from the Plan Team. The papers are development
studies rather than competing operational assessments.

::: {.callout-important}
The accepted ADMB assessment continues to provide current management advice.
RTMB, SPoRC, and Rceattle are being used to check the model calculations,
improve diagnostics, and evaluate options for future development. None is
proposed as a replacement assessment for September 2026.
:::

# Review package

| Report | Primary question | Role in the review |
|---|---|---|
| [**RTMB: main report**](ebs_pollock_rtmb_ebswp_assessment.html) | Can RTMB reproduce the base ADMB model, and what do its diagnostics and model alternatives show? | Main technical report and shared reference for comparing implementations |
| [**SPoRC: companion report**](https://jimianelli.github.io/sporc_ebswp/) | Can SPoRC reproduce the same base model and support different population-process structures? | Independent software comparison and continuing methods-development track |
| [**Rceattle: companion report**](https://noaa-afsc.github.io/ebswp_rceattle/) | Can Rceattle reproduce the main assessment dynamics and provide a practical foundation for future operational development? | Leading candidate for future operational development, after the remaining diagnostic and review work |

The [main RTMB report](ebs_pollock_rtmb_ebswp_assessment.html) provides the
most detail on the shared data definitions, checks made using the same
parameter values as ADMB, model fits, selectivity analyses, projections,
retrospectives, and uncertainty diagnostics. The SPoRC and Rceattle reports
show how the same assessment problem behaves in more general software
frameworks.

## Supporting analysis

| Identifier | Analysis | Role in the review |
|---|---|---|
| S-1 | [**Fishery selectivity alternatives**](appendix_fishery_selectivity.html) ([PDF](appendix_fishery_selectivity.pdf)) | Detailed RTMB comparison of the base, hierarchical double-logistic, and year-by-age AR1 fishery selectivity options; supports the selectivity discussion in the main RTMB report |

This analysis supports the RTMB report; it is not a fourth modeling
framework. The stable links allow all three reports to use the same equations,
diagnostics, and summary data.

# Where the results agree

The three reports reach several shared conclusions:

- All three comparisons use the base 2024 model with observed and predicted
  bottom-trawl survey age compositions evaluated over ages 1--15 and with the
  nominal multinomial sample sizes.
- When the same parameter values are used, the implementations closely
  reproduce the main ADMB population dynamics. This shows that the core model
  calculations have been transferred consistently.
- When each implementation estimates its own parameters, results differ
  because the parameterization, selectivity structure, and estimation methods
  differ.
- Time-varying fishery and survey selectivity remains an important source of
  sensitivity and some parameters remain weakly identified.
- Positive retrospective patterns require further evaluation before another
  framework is considered for operational use.
- Bayesian results remain exploratory until the chains mix adequately and
  effective sample sizes improve.

# How the frameworks differ

| Question | RTMB | SPoRC | Rceattle |
|---|---|---|---|
| What is it? | Direct RTMB representation of the base ADMB model | The same assessment expressed in a general single-region framework | The assessment expressed in a broader, extensible framework |
| Why is it useful? | Clear technical reference for checking calculations, diagnostics, and model changes | Independent check using different software and general population-process tools | Most promising route to a maintainable future operational model and broader extensions |
| What does it currently do well? | Detailed model-to-model checks, diagnostics, retrospectives, projections, and flexible selectivity development | Close reproduction of the base model, stable fits, and independent confirmation of the main dynamics | Close reproduction when parameter values are held fixed, an independently estimated comparison, general data and model architecture, and support for recruitment extensions |
| What work remains? | Retrospective bias and evaluation of candidate selectivity structures | Self-test failures, retrospective bias, and slow Bayesian mixing in the correlated survey-selectivity model | One weakly identified combination of annual selectivity parameters, retrospective bias, dependence on the observation model, and slow Bayesian mixing |
| Proposed use after this review | Keep as the technical reference and repeatable comparison test for later development | Continue as an independent methods and comparison track | Give priority as the operational-development candidate, after successful diagnostics, simulation testing, annual-update testing, and review |

# Proposed use of each framework

Each framework has a different development role. The proposed approach keeps
those roles while concentrating operational-development effort on Rceattle.

1. **Retain ADMB for management advice.** Continue the accepted operational
   assessment while candidate frameworks are evaluated.
2. **Retain RTMB as the technical reference.** Use the base RTMB
   implementation to check likelihood calculations, state variables,
   projections, and proposed structural changes.
3. **Continue SPoRC as an independent comparison.** Use SPoRC to test whether
   conclusions depend on a particular software architecture and to evaluate
   general process-model developments.
4. **Prioritize Rceattle for operational development.** Resolve selectivity
   identification and retrospective behavior, complete observation-model and
   simulation tests, demonstrate a reproducible annual update, and return with
   a clearly defined candidate model.
5. **Make any transition through formal review.** Present a future operational
   candidate only after the fitted model, uncertainty analysis,
   projections, and update procedures pass agreed review criteria.

# Questions for Plan Team discussion

The review would benefit from direction on the following questions:

1. Does the Plan Team agree that RTMB should serve as the implementation
   baseline while Rceattle receives priority for future operational
   development?
2. Which selectivity and observation-model sensitivities are essential before
   evaluating an operational Rceattle candidate?
3. What magnitude and pattern of retrospective bias would require model
   revision, additional uncertainty treatment, or rejection of a candidate?
4. Which simulation tests should be required to evaluate bias, estimability,
   and robustness under alternative recruitment and selectivity histories?
5. What evidence is needed to demonstrate that the annual data-update and
   projection procedures are ready for operational use?
6. At what review stage should posterior uncertainty be incorporated, given
   the current mixing limitations in candidate selectivity models?
